sections.title: INSTRUMENTS
sections.sub: what a strike sounds like · 28 labs

cards.name: CYMA-FORGE
cards.desc: Percussive cymatics: a Faraday hydro-tank, a biharmonic Chladni plate and an acoustic levitation field. Strike a plate and watch the sand find its nodes.

cards.name: CYMBAL-3D
cards.desc: A Föppl–von Kármán nonlinear plate with Weyl modal density — thousands of inharmonic modes summed into bronze. No pitch, no harmonics, just a plate whose modal spacing dissolves into shimmer at the edge and speaks in defined partials at the bell.

cards.name: CROTALES-3D
cards.desc: Chromatic antique cymbals as Chladni disk modes, struck or bowed at the edge. A small thick disk tuned to a definite pitch, which makes it the rare bronze instrument that can be played in a melody — and bowing the rim excites modes a strike cannot reach.

cards.name: PAN-3D
cards.desc: A steelpan and handpan whose note areas are tuned to 1:2:3 orthogonal mode coupling — the only struck object here that was designed to be harmonic rather than left inharmonic. Strike a note field and the overtone sits exactly where the tuner put it, which is why a pan sounds placed and a cymbal sounds found.

cards.name: KÁRMÁN-GONG 3D
cards.desc: Föppl–von Kármán nonlinear shell dynamics with wave turbulence and pitch glissando — a gong whose pitch bends as the shell deforms, which is why a struck gong blooms instead of simply ringing.

cards.name: KEISU-3D
cards.desc: A standing bell and a singing bowl: Rayleigh–Love rim modes plus Faraday spouting. Two ways a curved vessel sings — coupled rim modes in the metal, and a liquid film climbing and breaking from the wall.

cards.name: CAMPANA-3D
cards.desc: A free-free hanging bell resolved into its five named partials — hum, prime, tierce, quint and nominal — plus a bell swarm. The tierce sits a minor third above the prime, which is why a Western bell sounds minor whatever note you think you struck.

cards.name: TIMPANI-3D
cards.desc: A coupled kettle-cavity air spring, live pedal portamento and Bessel inharmonicity — the one percussion instrument that changes pitch while it is still ringing. The partials are not harmonic: roughly 1 : 1.59 : 2.14 : 2.30, which is why a timpanist tunes by ear and never by ratio.

cards.name: TAIKO-3D
cards.desc: A coupled dual-membrane wadaiko: two heads sharing one air column, with nonlinear pitch glide and kuchi-shōga vocal notation rendered as a WAV loop. The coupled heads are why a taiko's pitch bends under its own strike energy rather than settling where it started.

cards.name: SNARE-3D
cards.desc: A coupled membrane and snare-wire model with the PAS-40 rudiments built in. The wires are the interesting part: they are a stochastic nonlinear attachment, not a filter, so the buzz responds to how hard you hit and where — which is why a buzz roll and a marching rudiment sound like different instruments.

cards.name: CAVITY-KICK 3D
cards.desc: A bass drum as two resonators of equal standing: the head and the air inside it. Sweep the cavity volume through the head frequency and the two modes refuse to cross — they repel, with a minimum gap of 2g, and a visitor expecting an intersection hears two tones bounce off each other instead. The deepest fundamental in the suite, and the only lab where the air is the instrument.

cards.name: TALKING-DRUM 3D
cards.desc: An hourglass drum whose cord-laced head is squeezed under the arm to bend pitch continuously mid-strike — the only drum here whose pitch is played rather than set. The hourglass body is a coupled resonator, and the tension modulation is what lets a drum imitate a tonal language.

cards.name: DIAPASON-3D
cards.desc: A full-screen 3D Euler–Bernoulli tuning fork with von Mises stress and six eigenmodes — the geometry of a struck fork resolved into stress fields and the modes that follow from them.

cards.name: MARIMBA-3D
cards.desc: An arch-carved rosewood bar over a quarter-wave resonator tube, tuned so the second partial sits at 4x and the third at 10x the fundamental. A pan is tuned by hammering a plate; a bar is tuned by removing mass from underneath — same idea, opposite craft, and it is why wood sounds like wood.

cards.name: WATERPHONE-3D
cards.desc: A hydro-acoustic friction idiophone: a steel bowl, a column of water and a ring of tines. Tip it and the water redistributes, shifting every mode at once — a portamento with no moving part, driven by stick-slip and a fluid that is also the instrument.

cards.name: MATERIAL-SET 3D
cards.desc: One resonator, one geometry, seven materials - and only two numbers differ: speed of sound and internal damping. Because damping rises with frequency, high modes die first, so the spectrum collapses in brightness as it decays. That collapse is what you hear as warm. Bronze and wood differ not in pitch but in how fast their top end disappears.

cards.name: INVERSE-BAR 3D
cards.desc: Name a spectrum and the lab searches for a bar that produces it - the machine a marimba builder uses, run backwards. Ask for 1:4:10 and it returns a carving profile; run it twice from different seeds and get two visibly different bars with the same modes and the same sound. The shape is not the only thing that fits a spectrum, and this lab proves it.

cards.name: HETERO-THERE 3D
cards.desc: Two radio oscillators near 500 kHz and a difference you can hear. A hand near the rod changes capacitance, capacitance moves the oscillator, and the audio is the subtraction - never the carrier. The pitch mapping is brutally nonlinear, 32 cents per centimetre far out and over 400 near the rod, which is exactly why the instrument swoops. Toggle linearised and it becomes easy.

cards.name: RAINSTICK-3D
cards.desc: A granular avalanche through a pin lattice, with jamming as a real phase transition. The sound is not modal — it is a timing statistic: correlated cascades sound like rain, independent clicks sound like dust, and at high fill the flow stops entirely.

cards.name: PAS-40 STUDIO
cards.desc: V4.0: The forty Percussive Arts Society rudiments as an interactive simulator and sample lab. Pure technique, no physics — where the series started, and the ground everything else stands on.

cards.name: PENDULUM-LOOM
cards.desc: A 3D harmonic phase loom driven by Blackburn pendulums, Lissajous figures and coupled Huygens clocks — interference turned into rhythm. The most purely physical piece in the set: every hit traces back to a pendulum you can watch swing.

cards.name: NEWTON-PULSE 3D
cards.desc: A precision percussive Newton's cradle with an oddball mass chain, a zero-G BPM collider and a rhythm lab. Momentum transfer as rhythm — one ball in and two out is a musical decision, not just a physics demonstration.

cards.name: CHRONOCRYSTAL
cards.desc: 3D spectral graph percussion with a pendulum wave and a polyrhythmic automaton — a time crystal you can hear fold and unfold.

cards.name: EIGENPULSE
cards.desc: Spatial drumline drill and polyrhythmic hocket, visualised through Bessel-mode cymatics. Where a drill line meets an eigenmode.

cards.name: KAC-SPECTRA
cards.desc: Solve the inverse problem — can you hear the shape of a drum? An isospectral drum solver, a Poincaré hyperbolic tree and a Kuramoto chimera synth.

cards.name: QUASICRYSTAL-PU
cards.desc: Penrose aperiodic percussion — a tiling that never repeats, driven by a delta-rule state machine and a reversible automaton.

cards.name: PADIC-BRAID
cards.desc: Rhythm on a p-adic ultrametric tree, a non-holomorphic fractal series synth, and a braid group B₄ loom — where distance is not what you think.

cards.name: HYPER-SOLITON
cards.desc: A 4D polychoron projected through a Hopf fibration, struck as percussion, with a nonlinear Toda lattice carrying the transients.

cards.name: CHIMERA-SWARM
cards.desc: A 3D Kuramoto–Sakaguchi chimera manifold and swarmalator: one population locks in phase while another stays incoherent, and the boundary between them is what you hear.

cards.name: CAVITRON
cards.desc: Rayleigh–Plesset bubble collapse and sonoluminescence, a Rijke thermoacoustic flame tube, and shear-thickening impact rheology — three ways a strike becomes light and heat.

cards.name: METRONOME-SYNC 3D
cards.desc: Metronomes on a shared beam that synchronise through nothing but their own recoil — Huygens' 1665 observation, integrated rather than scripted. Two identical metronomes settle into ANTI-PHASE, not unison: they alternate, and the double-time pulse on the interval histogram is the physics telling you so. Sweep the coupling and watch the order parameter cross over.

cards.name: BEAT-FIELD 3D
cards.desc: Two pulse trains and one piece of arithmetic. Detune them and the beat rate becomes a tempo; set them to 3:2 and you get a hemiola that never drifts. Then sweep the master tempo past 20 Hz and the same ratio stops being a cross-rhythm and becomes a chord — a perfect fifth at 702 cents, from the identical integers.

cards.name: SAND-PILE 3D
cards.desc: A Bak–Tang–Wiesenfeld pile that grows until it collapses, and the collapse onsets are the beat. No tempo is set — the rhythm is the pile's own instability, bursty and clustered with quiet refractory gaps. Flip to the Poisson null and the difference is instant: human musical timing is 1/f too, which is why a grid sounds stiff and a pile does not.

cards.name: DRIP-CLOCK 3D
cards.desc: A dripping faucet as a rhythm you can derive on paper: Tate’s law gives the drop mass, so the tempo is set by surface tension, neck radius and flow, to within a few percent. Sweep the flow and the drip stops being metronomic: period-2 is swing, then period-4, then deterministic chaos, then jetting. The only lab here whose tempo has a closed form, and it still finds a way to break it.

cards.name: STRANGE-DRUM 3D
cards.desc: A chaotic oscillator sampled through a threshold plane, so the orbit becomes a groove. The same seed always replays the identical rhythm, yet nothing predicts the thousandth hit without iterating to it. Sweep the parameter through period-doubling into chaos, linger in the intermittency window where it sounds like a player varying a pattern, then hit Shuffle and hear the order vanish while the histogram stays identical.

cards.name: SPIRAL-DRUM 3D
cards.desc: A FitzHugh-Nagumo excitable medium with a phase singularity in it: the wavefront curls and rotates, and one revolution is one beat. The tempo is set by the refractory tail, so a spiral cannot spin faster than its own tail decays. Push the excitability and the tip stops tracing a clean circle, starts meandering, then goes chaotic, and the beat degrades with it. Nothing random was added.

cards.name: JAM-WAVE 3D
cards.desc: Cars on a ring road obeying four rules, with nobody in charge. Past a critical density, stop-and-go jams nucleate out of nothing and travel backwards against the traffic, so a roadside observer hears burst-quiet-burst. Set the dawdle probability to zero and every jam vanishes at the same density: congestion needs noise to start, yet is not itself noise.

cards.name: GRAPH-CHOIR 3D
cards.desc: V2.0: Kuramoto oscillators wired into a graph, where the topology decides which rhythms are even possible. Wind a phase gradient around a loop and it locks into a rotating pattern — a polyrhythm carried by a quantised winding number that cannot be halved. Rewire the same nodes into a tree and every twist collapses to unison, because a graph with no cycles has nowhere to put one.

cards.name: SLAB-RELEASE 3D
cards.desc: A cohesive slab on a weak layer, and nothing happens until shear stress beats shear strength. Then a crown crack runs upslope at 48 m/s ahead of the debris, which follows a Voellmy deceleration into the runout. The first lab here whose sound is a continuous event rather than an onset - and the first whose null is silence.

cards.name: CRASHING-WAVE 3D
cards.desc: Falling water is silent. The roar of a breaking wave is entrained air - the crest traps a void, the void shatters into bubbles, and each bubble rings at its Minnaert frequency. Change only the seabed slope and the same wave goes from a hiss to a thud, because a plunging break swallows bigger air. Below Miche’s index of 0.78, nothing happens at all.

cards.name: THUNDER 3D
cards.desc: The only shock wave in the suite. A channel at 30,000 K expands supersonically and radiates an N-wave whose rise time grows as the square root of distance - a linear source would keep its shape. And the roll you hear is not reverb: a bolt kilometres long arrives in pieces, so the rumble is the shape of the channel.

cards.name: SEICHE-TANK 3D
cards.desc: A bounded basin has a natural frequency: T = 2L/√(gh). Drive a tank at that period and the slosh grows until it breaks at the antinodes; drive it 40% off and the water barely moves. The middle stays still while the ends rise, and moving the listener from node to antinode makes the tempo appear or vanish.

cards.name: CALVE 3D
cards.desc: A crevasse races through the ice at 1.5 kHz and up. Then the block falls, and the silence between the crack and the boom is exactly the time it takes - √(2h/g). For a 50 m cliff that is 3.2 seconds between a rifle shot and a thud, and no other lab here has a gap you can measure.

cards.name: SEISMOGRAM 3D
cards.desc: An earthquake arrives in three phases, and the gap between the first two is a ruler: Δt = d(1/vₛ − 1/vₚ), about 0.119 s per kilometre. Move the epicentre and the same event becomes a different rhythm - three sharp hits nearby, a minute-long swell at 500 km. The only sound here that tells you how far away it happened.

cards.name: BLAST-RADIUS 3D
cards.desc: A point explosion has only two quantities to work with, energy and air density, so the fireball radius can only be R = ξ(E/ρ)^(1/5)t^(2/5). Fallout of units alone. Double the yield and the fireball grows 15% - and a constant-velocity puff, which is what a wrong model produces, gives slope 1.00 instead of 0.40.

cards.name: BOOM-CARPET 3D
cards.desc: A supersonic aircraft drags a cone, and the boom reaches you when that cone sweeps past - from a direction the aircraft has already left. Inside the carpet you hear a double N-wave separated by L/v; one metre outside it, silence, with the aircraft plainly overhead. The only lab here where the direction of the sound encodes a velocity.

sections.title: PERCEPTION & CAPSTONE
sections.sub: about the suite, not inside it · 3 labs

cards.name: COCHLEA-MASK 3D
cards.desc: The listener, finally: auditory masking thresholds and pitch perception. One hit can hide another that is louder, and where the threshold sits depends on frequency, time and bandwidth. Every other lab asks how an object vibrates; this one asks what you can actually hear of it.

cards.name: TIMBRE-CLOCK 3D
cards.desc: One array of partials and one dial. V2.0: at audio rate the array is a chord; slow it a thousandfold and the identical numbers become a rhythm you can count. Sweep through 20 to 50 Hz and hear repetition fuse into pitch, then load a cymbal and find that the shimmer becomes a jumble nobody could tap along to.

cards.name: ROOM-TONE 3D
cards.desc: V2.0: the space every other lab sits in, now in true stereo with ear spacing, first-order wall reflections and a volumetric standing-wave view. Below the Schroeder frequency a room has discrete modes you hear as boom; above it, only decay. Drag the volume down and the crossover climbs - so a small room is MORE coloured than a large one, which is the opposite of what everyone expects.

cards.name: STROKE-LAB 3D
cards.desc: The first lab whose limiting physics is the player. A stroke is a driven spring-mass-damper with a rebound, and the arm tops out around ten per second - until the grip loosens and the stick is allowed to come back. A drum roll was never fast single strokes; it was letting physics do half the work.

cards.name: BEAT-FORGE 3D
cards.desc: Beat architecture as mathematics: Euclidean necklaces distributing hits as evenly as a rhythm allows, microtiming that decides whether a groove sits or swings, and polyrhythms that lock only at the least common multiple. The first lab here about when a hit happens rather than what it sounds like.

cards.name: PHASE-LOOP 3D
cards.desc: Write one bar, choose one integer, and the piece writes itself. Two identical voices at n and n+1 drift apart, dissolve into a jumble at the halfway point, and snap back into unison displaced by a single beat at exactly cycle n. Nothing after the first bar is authored - the arrival is arithmetic, and it is computable to the sample.

cards.name: AKSAK-FORGE 3D
cards.desc: Seven beats divided as 2+2+3 is a different piece from 3+2+2, at identical tempo and identical hit count. The partition is the composition, and nothing else changes. Split and merge groups on a segmented ring, then set the accents flat and hear the metre vanish into seven identical beats.
